title: The PHP Security Model
learning_outcomes: Explain what the php security model contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: trust boundaries.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on trust boundaries; then compare it with defense in depth. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use the php security model when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For the php security model, begin with trust boundaries. Also distinguish defense in depth; least privilege; security configuration. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.text: Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for the php security model from top to bottom. Start by identifying trust boundaries, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for the php security model that demonstrates "trust boundaries". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.

hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.

summary: The PHP Security Model is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
